title: 249 bots, 2,468 closed trades, profit factor 0.38. Down $392k. Here's the whole dashboard.
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
I've been running a paper fleet for about a month to stress-test a backtesting engine I'm building. 249 bots across 5 desks, everything on real quotes, no real money.

It's down $392,286 all-time. 42% win rate, profit factor 0.38 — so for every dollar it lost it made 38 cents back. Worst single day was −$173,070. Right now there's $5.29M of open risk sitting across 224 positions.

Recording is the whole thing, unedited. Desks, open trades, closed trades, the bots, the live terminal. I didn't cut out the red.

Two things I've actually learned from it, in case they're useful to anyone else:

A 42% win rate isn't the problem. Profit factor 0.38 is. The losers are roughly two and a half times the winners and no hit rate fixes that.

And open risk is the number I wasn't watching. $5.29M exposed against equity that's already down — I'd been looking at realised P&L, which tells you what already happened rather than what can still happen to you.

Genuinely curious what you'd look at first with a fleet this size. My instinct is that most of these bots are the same trade wearing different names, and the concentration is doing more damage than any single strategy.

Institutions trade on mostly knowledge with a little bit of technical to understand the economics of it. 

How does your fleet handle fundamentals?
